text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but the bigger story is the sharp 4.7% drop from its peak on September 15th. Oil prices fell sharply on September 17th after Saudi Arabia signaled it would increase crude exports through the Hormuz Strait following a pipeline attack, easing supply concerns that had driven prices higher. Additionally, comments from Trump suggesting the U.S. may be nearing an end to its Iran conflict reduced geopolitical risk premium in oil markets, further pressuring prices downward. The stock has been caught in this reversal—trading at $132.97 today versus $141.22 just two days ago.

The weakness also reflects broader concern about what sustained high energy costs mean for the U.S. economy; reports on September 17th highlighted how record diesel prices are already hitting transportation and could spread pain through other sectors if they persist. For an oil company, the worry is that recession fears from runaway energy costs could ultimately hurt energy demand, offsetting any near-term benefit from higher prices.
